name: Brilliant
tagline: Build interactive practice around user-authored math and science lessons

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: First 2 levels of every course; up to 2 lessons/day; sequential progress; occasional ads

tiers.name: Premium Individual
tiers.limits: Unlimited lessons and all levels across 40+ courses; no ads; jump ahead; Koji tutoring
tiers.notes: Annual plan is billed $240 once per year.

tiers.name: Premium Family
tiers.limits: Up to 6 seats; each member gets a separate Premium account; all 40+ courses
tiers.notes: The live subscription flow presents this as an annual-renewing flat-price household plan.

tiers.name: Premium Group
tiers.limits: 3–50 seats; starts at 3 seats for $33.99/month equivalent; each extra seat $10.10/month
tiers.notes: Annual only and billed as one payment; the displayed per-user figure is the 3-seat starting rate.

pricing.freeTierCaps: First 2 levels of every course and up to 2 lessons/day; sequential progress; occasional ads
pricing.billingTerms: Individual monthly + annual; Family annual; Group annual only; subscriptions auto-renew
pricing.hiddenCosts: Group plan has a 3-seat minimum; extra seats cost $10.10/month each and a full group cannot add seats mid-term, capacity can be increased at renewal.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Brilliant, build interactive practice around user-authored math and science lessons. The hard boundary is expert curriculum, interactive problem library, pedagogy, apps, and content rights, plus content, pedagogy, and network.
coreLoopDIY: Turn user-authored math and science lessons into a study plan with interactive practice, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
requirements: optional speech or language-model API key
whatYouLose: expert curriculum, interactive problem library, pedagogy, apps, and content rights
ongoingBurden: curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Brilliant because the learning loop is buildable, while trusted curriculum, instructors, feedback, credentials, and community are not. The recurring cost buys curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Moodle
priorArt.desc: Long-running open-source learning platform with courses, assessments, and progress tracking.

alternatives.name: eXeLearning
alternatives.desc: A desktop lesson authoring tool for interactive exercises, games, equations and quizzes, with decidedly public-sector aesthetics.

facts.install: Desktop installer or local browser PWA; the Team Edition is separately self-hosted
facts.dataFormat: Editable lessons live as .elpx project files; output exports as web pages, EPUB3 or SCORM/LMS packages, while Team Edition uses server storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is an authoring and export tool, not Brilliant's polished ready-made adaptive STEM curriculum, guided learning path or motivation system.

alternatives.name: Oppia
alternatives.desc: Authors branching interactive explorations that respond to wrong answers instead of merely displaying the solution.

facts.install: Use Oppia.org directly, or deploy the Python and Angular application on a Google App Engine-style stack
facts.dataFormat: Explorations, skills, stories, questions and learner progress live in Oppia's hosted Google Cloud Datastore and Storage, or the equivalent self-hosted deployment
facts.gapVsPaid: Creating responsive branches is manual, and the result does not match Brilliant's broad authored catalog or production-quality interactive visuals.
facts.setupBlocker: None on Oppia.org; self-hosting is a developer-grade Google App Engine deployment

alternatives.name: Lumi
alternatives.desc: A free desktop H5P editor for interactive lessons, simulations and quizzes; content quality remains your problem.

facts.install: Windows Store or EXE, macOS Intel or Apple-silicon DMG, or Linux Snap, AppImage, deb or pacman package
facts.dataFormat: Interactive content lives in local .h5p packages and can be exported as H5P, standalone HTML or SCORM
facts.gapVsPaid: It edits standalone H5P activities but supplies no sequenced curriculum, adaptive guided path or ready-made STEM library.
facts.setupBlocker: Windows may show SmartScreen, and current macOS builds have had unsigned or damaged-app Gatekeeper reports

alternatives.name: GeoGebra
alternatives.desc: Excellent interactive mathematics authoring and practice, but it stops being Brilliant once the science is not mathematical.

facts.install: Use the hosted web apps or install native desktop or mobile apps
facts.dataFormat: Activities can be saved locally as .ggb ZIP/XML files or to a GeoGebra cloud account as online resources
facts.gapVsPaid: It is excellent for interactive mathematics but becomes a much weaker substitute once the science is not mathematical, and it lacks Brilliant's guided curriculum.

alternatives.name: Moodle
alternatives.desc: Hosts authored activities, quizzes and progress, although the actual interactive pedagogy still has to come from you.

facts.install: Install PHP and a supported database and web server, create the moodledata directory, then run the web installer and cron
facts.dataFormat: Course records and activity data live in a relational database; uploaded files, caches and sessions live under moodledata, with .mbz course backups
facts.gapVsPaid: It is an LMS shell rather than Brilliant's interactive pedagogy, so the author must build the lessons, feedback and activities from scratch.
facts.setupBlocker: Web hosting, PHP and database compatibility, cron, security hardening and upgrades all belong to the operator

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal study companion DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Brilliant in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and a service worker for offline use; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: turn user-authored math and science lessons into a study plan with interactive practice, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Import Markdown, text, or user-authored notes and split them into editable learning units.
Create flashcards and short quizzes only after showing the generated items for approval.
Implement a transparent spaced-repetition schedule with due, again, hard, good, and easy actions.
Add goals, study sessions, streak-free progress charts, notes, and weak-topic review.
For language practice, record the learner and compare timing or pronunciation without presenting medical claims.
Support offline use, full export, reset, backup, and deletion of all learning data.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out licensed premium courses.
Deliberately leave out accredited certificates and grading.
Deliberately leave out live tutors, large classrooms, and a learner marketplace.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
